bio: I'm Damon Lin, a CS student who believes the best way to learn is to build. I run Hack Club at my school, lead a competitive robotics team, and spend my weekends at hackathons turning half-baked ideas into working software before the deadline hits.

What got me into code wasn't a class — it was the feeling of shipping something real. A dashboard that scouts robotics matches. A web app that helps my team coordinate. A game built in 12 hours with friends. Every project taught me more than any tutorial ever could.
When I'm not coding, I'm probably organizing a workshop, mentoring newer hackers, or arguing about tabs vs. spaces.

values.title: Build in Public
values.description: Shipping beats perfection. Every project, even the broken ones, teaches something worth sharing.

values.title: Community First
values.description: The best code in the world is useless if nobody uses it. Building communities around technology is the real multiplier.

values.title: Learn by Doing
values.description: Tutorials teach syntax. Projects teach engineering. The only way to grow is to build things that scare you a little.
